messages:
sara: FYI we started seeing a p95 latency spike on qwen2.5 hosted endpoints around 01:58 UTC, affects long-context workloads (>8k). noticed after kernel-selector rollout.
liam: copy, any deploy IDs or config changes?
sara: @deploy-bot rolled kernel-selector v2.3 at 01:58. config snippet: `autokernel=true prefer_fused=true kernel_switch_cooldown=0s`.
jess: ran a quick sample against the production traces. KV cache hit rate dropped, and profiler shows a lot more kernel_switch events. suspecting kernel churn + batch scheduler interactions.
liam: can you paste the selector logs?
jess: sure — here's the relevant fragment from the runtime logs (trimmed):
```
[01:59:12] kernel_select: model=qwen2.5 ctx=16384 chosen=matmul_fused_v2
[01:59:12] kernel_switch: fallback=matmul_generic reason=kv_stride_mismatch
[01:59:12] kernel_select: model=qwen2.5 ctx=16384 chosen=matmul_generic
[01:59:13] kernel_select: model=qwen2.5 ctx=2048 chosen=matmul_fused_v2
[01:59:13] kernel_switch: fallback=matmul_generic reason=kv_head_misaligned
```

jess: profiler aggregate (1k requests, mixed multi-ling prompts):
```
p50_before: 65ms  -> 80ms
p95_before: 420ms -> 615ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.92 -> 0.58
kernel_switch_rate: 0.02 -> 0.18
batch_wait_avg: 3.2ms -> 12.8ms
```

andrew: i reproduced locally with a zh+en mixed prompt set. tokenizer split boundaries change for certain utf8 sequences, which shifts tokenization and effectively changes KV indexing for in-flight requests. when kernel selector swaps kernels mid-request the KV offsets don't line up with the new kernel's expected layout -> extra memreads and cache misses.
liam: interesting — so this is a confluence: tokenizer variability (multi-ling), autokernel switching, and batching heuristics that assume stable kv indices. explains both the increased kernel_switch_rate and lower kv hit rate.
sara: do we have repro steps for a focused micro-benchmark? want to test mitigations before rolling back.
jess: yes, here's a repro command I used locally:
```
# run 1k requests with long ctx and mixed zh/en prompts
tools/bench/throughput --model qwen2.5 --ctx 16384 --batch 1 --requests 1000 --prompts samples/multilang_zh_en.json --enable-autokernel=true --kernel-selector v2.3
```

jess: also captured a short flamegraph snippet that shows repeated memcpy/kv_lookup spikes aligned with kernel_switch events. i'll upload to the perf bucket.
perf-bot: Canary scheduled: dedicated-pool-3, 10% traffic, start=2060123600, duration=15m — running kernel-selector=v2.2 for qwen2.5-largecontext.
liam: my proposed mitigations (short term):
- disable autokernel for qwen2.5 when ctx >= 8192 (autokernel=false for that profile)
- enforce kernel_switch_cooldown=30s to avoid churn during a single request group
- add a pre-check in selector: verify kv_layout_compat(model, chosen_kernel) before switching

jess: long term: update batching heuristic to pin KV layout per-request and avoid mixing tokens that change tokenizer segmentation mid-batch; also add tokenization canonicalization for mixed-script prompts to reduce fragmentation.
andrew: i can try a small patch that normalizes unicode NFKC for tokenizer when multi-script is detected; should reduce boundary drift in many cases. will bench impact on token counts.
sara: roll plan?
liam: immediate: roll kernel-selector config to v2.2 on prod for qwen2.5-largecontext profiles (perf-bot can apply). medium: push selector patch with kv_layout guard and cooldown. long: batching changes + tokenizer normalization.
sara: ok please coordinate. jess — run the canary results and drop a summary in this thread. add a one-liner to the incident board if p95 doesn't return to baseline after rollback. :thumbsup:
jess: will do, starting the canary run and collecting graphs. tagging @andrew for tokenizer patch follow-up. :eyes:
perf-bot: Canary completed at 2060123700. p95 returned to 430ms on canary (close to baseline). full rollout paused pending selector patch.
liam: nice. i'll open a PR with the cooldown + kv_layout check and link the perf numbers.
sara: thanks team — good catch. we'll keep this thread for follow-ups.
